records.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit ONLY image 3, the Qianyang two-view character sheet. Images 1 and 2 remain direct production style references. Preserve the exact same handsome 20-year-old face, expression, sand-brown hair and dark side patch, two ram horns, sage/cream jacket, navy sash, wool regions, trousers, shoes and long brown horse tail in BOTH views.
Anatomy correction: each view must have EXACTLY TWO EARS TOTAL, and both are the long horizontal SHEEP EARS. KEEP the long sheep ears completely unchanged. REMOVE the additional small HUMAN EAR pinnae currently visible beside the cheeks below the hair. Cover those former human-ear locations with simple solid sand-brown/charcoal hair blocks and smooth warm-peach side-of-head contours, so there are NO visible human ear openings or pinnae. The two sheep ears are the character's only ears. Do not remove horns or sheep ears, do not add accessories.
Framing correction: scale BOTH existing full-body figures down about 8 percent together on a sufficiently wide transparent canvas so every horn tip, foot and long horse-tail tip has clear transparent space, especially the rightmost horse-tail tip. Keep the entire one horse tail per figure, no cropping and no second tail. Keep front + three-quarter views and their matching identity.
Use the production masters' simple near-black variable outline, sparse internal lines, flat matte colors and hard-edged shadows. Flat amber iris + black pupil, no eye highlights. True transparent alpha background, no labels, letters, scenery, glow or cast shadow. Make only ear anatomy and margin corrections; no redesign.

review.summary: The requested ear correction hides the frontal human pinnae under hair; a small apparent human pinna still remains behind the cheek in the three-quarter view. Sheep horns, sheep ears and horse tail remain consistent, but the no-extra-ear requirement is not fully passed.

threeQuarter.additionalHumanPinnaeVisible: 1 suspected small pinna remains behind cheek

sourceTraitsVisible: Sheep-like organic horns/ears and wool regions.
Long hanging horse-hair tail visible behind legs in front and beside hip in three-quarter.
limitations: Unresolved extra-ear anatomy in three-quarter view. Do not mark character qualified or publish to website.
Margin improved: alpha >=128 bounding box (129,31,1260,1171) on a 1312x1199 canvas; tail is inside the frame with 52px right margin.
Wool can still read as fur cuff rather than skin-grown wool.
Exact curled horn shape, palette, human age/gender and profession are original inventions, not stated by the source.
Facial line density is reduced by full-body framing; additional head detail sheet may be useful later.
Some hair and cloth shading is finer than the production portraits; remains candidate, not accepted final.

historicalAssets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Transparent original anime yokai character asset, ONE character shown twice: front view on the left and three-quarter view on the right. Use both attached production PNGs DIRECTLY as the drawing-style masters: match their natural expressive anime brows and mouth shapes, warm peach face skin, near-black variable-width contour, sparse interior lines, clean flat matte color and hard-edged cel shadows. A flat single-color iris and pure black pupil, NO catchlights and NO iris textures. Simple chunky hair masses. Human beauty and lively expression; no elderly face, burly man, photorealism, painterly game concept art, airbrush gradients, intricate shiny hair, neon, glow or mist. These references control drawing technique, NOT face identity, accessories or clothes: do not copy goggles, hoodie, brown bob or the existing reference faces. No names, labels, text, panels or decorative framing. Truly alpha-transparent background.
Subject SHJ-042 Qianyang: a handsome 20-year-old young man with a slender athletic human figure and distinctly organic SHEEP traits combined with ONE HORSE TAIL. Short warm sand-brown wavy hair in only a few chunky shapes, one dark charcoal undercut patch above his left ear, straight dark brows and matte amber eyes. Alert slightly annoyed open mouth, defined youthful jaw; not the same face as image 1. Two ivory ram horns grow directly from the temples, curling tightly backward around two long sideways sheep ears. Small areas of cream wool grow directly along neck and forearms, not a fur stole or costume. ONE long dark brown horse tail emerges naturally from the lower spine and falls in a plain coarse hair mass to calf length, clearly visible beside his body in BOTH views. It must be a horse's long straight hanging hair tail, NOT a fluffy sheep or fox tail.
Clothes: simple muted sage-green short wrap jacket with cream inner collar and dark navy cloth waist sash, charcoal cropped trousers and plain low brown shoes. The jacket has modest openings that make the organic neck wool and forearm wool visible. No ornaments, weapons, letters or patterns. One hand rests near the waist, the other hangs naturally; the two views share exactly the same face, horns, ear count, hair patch, garment cut and palette.
Full-body head-to-toe composition for BOTH views, side by side with clear separation. Two horns, two sheep ears, two human arms, two legs and exactly one visible horse tail per view. Keep all horn tips, shoes and entire horse tail inside frame with generous margin. Clearly different front and three-quarter angles. Reduce detail to the production portraits' sparse line density; no dense fleece texture.

review.summary: Front and three-quarter versions visibly preserve the same young face, sand-brown hair with dark side patch, paired ram horns and sheep ears, sage/cream wrap jacket, navy sash, dark trousers and long brown horse tail.
sourceTraitsVisible: Sheep-like organic horns/ears and wool regions.
Long hanging horse-hair tail visible behind legs in front and beside hip in three-quarter.
limitations: Extra human ear pinnae appear alongside sheep ears in both views; four-ear anatomy is unsupported and triggered R02 correction.
Wool around sleeves can read as fur cuffs; skull-grown horns/ears and lower-spine tail establish organic fusion, but wool/skin transition needs style review.
Exact curled horn shape, palette, human age/gender and profession are original inventions, not stated by the source.
Facial line density is reduced by full-body framing; additional head detail sheet may be useful later.
Some hair and cloth shading is finer than the production portraits; remains candidate, not accepted final.

Subject SHJ-043 Tongqu: a beautiful 19-year-old young woman with a slim youthful HUMAN face and organic BLACK PHEASANT BODY TRAITS and RED BIRD FEET. Her jaw-length charcoal-black hair is an angular swept side cut, with one slim longer lock tucked behind the left side; do not copy reference woman's brown bob. Narrow matte muted olive eyes, sharp uneven brows and a terse slightly open mouth; assertive rather than placid. Her face and human hands stay warm peach. Small black feather ears and a compact black crest grow from her head, NOT a feather hair accessory. Black plumage grows organically over the shoulders and upper arms; a few layered black feather blades emerge from each forearm; a single long narrow black pheasant tail grows from lower back. Render feathers as only a few broad, readable near-black shapes, no etched feather texture.
Most important source trait: her TWO lower legs from just below the knees transform into genuine exposed VERMILION-RED scaly BIRD SHANKS and RED THREE-TOED BIRD FEET with small dark claws. These are her actual red skin/scales/toes, NOT red boots, shoes, socks, tights or armor. Both red feet must be fully visible in BOTH views. Upper body is youthful and human; do not replace her face with a bird head.
Clothes: simple cream short cross-collar jacket with black edging over a dark sleeveless base and modest charcoal knee-length divided skirt, a narrow brick-red cloth waist sash. Open forearms reveal organic black feathers. Human hands relaxed at sides. No weapon, jewelry, badges or decorative panels. Same face, side cut, black feathers, vermilion shanks, tail, clothes and palette across both angles.
Full-body front and three-quarter, both head-to-toe within the frame, plenty of margin below every red toe and around tail. Let the three-quarter view reveal the tail root and side feathers clearly. Each version has one head, two human arms/hands, two legs ending in red bird feet and one pheasant tail. Sparse near-black contours and simple flat colors; prioritize readable red anatomy over fabric detail.
